correctness.rationale: There are 4·3² oriented edges and the complement of a middle letter has no fixed point, so there are 18 target orbits. Tabulating quotient incidences yields four vertices of degree 3 and four of degree 6, with only the two stated alternating classes joining distinct odd vertices. A complete walk using 18 windows cannot have four odd vertices; at 19 windows the one extra edge must remove two odd vertices. For a closed walk at least two extras are necessary; at 20 windows their endpoints must be the four distinct odd vertices. This proves the lower bounds and the stated rigidity, not by assuming quotient walks always lift. Scans of the actual oriented witnesses give lengths 21 and 20, full coverage and the claimed multiplicities. Independent exhaustive replay works in the oriented overlap graph and permits any two surplus transitions, including two repeats of the same class; a complete walk of at most 20 steps cannot have more. It finds zero complete 18-window paths and zero 19-window closed walks, 57,984 linear optima with a 28,992-per-repeat split, and 289,920 indexed circular optima with the required repeat profile. The 18 distinct classes rule out any proper period of a 20-letter circle, so dividing by 20 gives 14,496 rotational optima. The remaining odd vertices of a linear optimum are singleton classes with a unique oriented closing edge; the reverse operation cuts one of the four repeated-class windows of the primitive optimum circle.
residual_risks: Enumeration is exhaustive only for the specified four labeled letters and three-letter windows. The quotient argument establishes parity necessities; existence and the census use oriented walks.

value.rationale: Order three with a fixed four-letter pairing and a uniform adjacent-equality prohibition gives a natural small covering problem. Unlike the unrestricted odd-order model, the orbit-count lower bound fails, and the amount and placement of the extra windows differ for open and closed hosts. The exact counts and cut/close relation describe how much choice really remains after enforcing both strand insensitivity and adjacency avoidance. They supply reproducible benchmarks for restricted universal-cover constructions, not a biological efficacy claim.
residual_risks: No claim for longer windows, larger alphabets or empirical binding, synthesis or sequencing performance.
